Get the bivariate residuals: the association between pairs of indicators that each class leaves unexplained

Source: R/wildcards.R
get_residuals.Rd

get_residuals() returns the bivariate residuals, a check of local independence: for each pair of indicators within each class, the association that the model leaves unexplained.

Usage

get_residuals(x)

Arguments

x

One of:

  • a profile, class or transition fit as described above. The table is the one diagnostics() computes with its defaults, which assesses each class separately;

  • an enumeration grid of such fits. The tables of the fitted candidates are stacked, with a first column candidate;

  • the result of diagnostics(). The table is the one the result holds, so diagnostics(fit, by = "overall") gives the residuals pooled over the classes.

Value

A data frame with one row per class and pair of indicators (and per candidate for a grid) and the columns:

  • profile: the class, as profile_1, profile_2, ...; overall for residuals pooled over the classes;

  • indicator_1, indicator_2: the pair;

  • kind: the kind of pair, as listed above;

  • observed, expected: the observed association and the one the model implies;

  • residual: the residual association;

  • effective_n: the effective number of units behind it;

  • statistic, df, p_value: the test, NA where there is none;

  • p_adjusted: the p-value adjusted across the pairs.

Errors: latents_bad_argument when the fit is of a family without bivariate residuals (a mixture regression, a growth mixture, an additive or cross-level fit, or a general transition fit of class multilpa_lta), and when no candidate of a grid has them; the message names the tables the object does have. latents_unsupported_noise when the fit has a noise component. latents_not_a_fit when x is not a fit, a grid or a diagnostics result.

Details

The statistic depends on the two indicators (column kind):

  • "gaussian", two continuous indicators: the residual correlation, with a normal test;

  • "categorical", two categorical or ordinal indicators: a chi-square test of the observed two-way table against the one the model expects;

  • "mixed" or "count", a continuous with a categorical indicator or a pair with a count indicator: a correlation, without a test.

The p-values are adjusted across the pairs by the Benjamini-Hochberg method. A fit with sampling weights reports the associations without tests. ?get_results describes the statistics in full.

Only profile, class and transition fits have these residuals: fits of lpa(), lca(), multilpa() and multilca(), with or without covariates, and transition fits of lta() of class multilpa_transitions.

See also

get_results() for the statistics; diagnostics() and get_checks() for the check that reads this table.

Examples

fit <- lca(student_esm, c("time_with_friends", "on_social_media", "sports"),
           n_classes = 2, n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
get_residuals(fit)
#>     profile       indicator_1     indicator_2        kind     observed
#> 1 profile_2 time_with_friends          sports categorical 7.373151e-02
#> 2 profile_1 time_with_friends          sports categorical 1.695573e-02
#> 3 profile_1   on_social_media          sports categorical 7.743261e-04
#> 4 profile_1 time_with_friends on_social_media categorical 4.846465e-04
#> 5 profile_2   on_social_media          sports categorical 4.268376e-05
#> 6 profile_2 time_with_friends on_social_media categorical 2.674778e-05
#>       expected     residual effective_n    statistic df    p_value p_adjusted
#> 1 0.000000e+00 7.373151e-02    740.9499 4.028016e+00  1 0.04475055  0.2685033
#> 2 3.454893e-17 1.695573e-02   1841.0501 5.292958e-01  1 0.46690306  0.9994096
#> 3 5.529567e-17 7.743261e-04   1841.0501 1.115166e-03  1 0.97336032  0.9994096
#> 4 1.349080e-16 4.846465e-04   1841.0501 4.427385e-04  1 0.98321267  0.9994096
#> 5 1.577941e-16 4.268376e-05    740.9499 1.366123e-06  1 0.99906742  0.9994096
